note: Orchestrator (Opus) re-read of all 20 CONTROL_CONTRAST verdicts on regex-flagged observations, 2026-09-19. RULE APPLIED: the verdict stands only if the adjudicator's own cited quote NAMES a healthy / normal / unaffected / non-diseased comparator. The readers systematically inferred an unstated comparator -- one batch's own summary says '(implied vs healthy)' three times -- which the task instructions forbade. Four verdicts stand and were genuine gaps in the CONTROL regex; that regex has been widened accordingly. Only CONTROL_CONTRAST verdicts were re-read: overturning an adjudicator toward the finding while leaving the other direction unchecked would bias the estimate, so the SUBGROUP_ONLY verdicts are re-checked separately by the widened regex, which reclassifies any observation whose sentences do name a control. REVIEW WAS RUN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, to remove exactly that bias: all 18 surviving SUBGROUP_ONLY verdicts were re-read under the same strict rule and NONE was overturned -- every one cites a quote naming a within-disease subgroup (Ab+ vs Ab- cognitively normal, sALS vs bALS, SCI severity grade, MS genetic-risk cluster, antibiotic-exposed subgroup, rifaximin arm, body-first PD), an animal arm, or a pre/post comparison. So the correction runs one way because only one direction was wrong, not because only one was checked.
